content: We need to determine number of methyl groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can get NMR spectra to infer. Use proton NMR to see methyl signals (singlet, doublet, etc). Could also use carbon NMR to see CH3 carbons. Probably easiest: get proton NMR spectra via tool. Then count distinct methyl signals (CH3). But need to be careful: overlapping signals may be same type. However question likely expects count of methyl groups present. Use proton NMR to identify number of methyl resonances. Could also use carbon NMR to count CH3 carbons. Let's get proton NMR.
